sentences_over_45.text: Application records joined with bureau histories, previous-loan behaviour and transaction aggregates at several depths and time windows yield hundreds to thousands of candidate predictors observed on hundreds of thousands to millions of decisions, many of the predictors redundant, some unstable over time and a few unavailable at the moment a lending decision is taken .

Supervised selectors are refitted in every validation fold and at every model refresh, and their cost grows with the number of decisions and, for redundancy-aware selectors, with the number of candidates over which redundancy is computed: on the first development fold of Stability 2024, one mRMR pass took 522 seconds over the 1,959-feature universe and 21 seconds over a 100-feature pool.

First, a held-out comparison, temporal for LendingClub and Stability 2024 and recency-shifted for Home Credit, of classical, model-based and LLM pre-screened selection, whose semantic stage reads no data rows, across three credit portfolios of up to 1,959 engineered features and 1.5 million decisions (1,526,659) and two backbones; the six paired HO comparisons between the methods with the highest observed HO AUC in each family are reported as effect sizes with paired bootstrap intervals, and repeated under two further leader-choice rules, one of which uses no held-out information to choose the compared methods.

Section  REF reviews related work, Section  REF gives background, Sections  REF and REF specify the methods and the experimental setup, and Section  REF reports the results in the order of the questions a reader is likely to ask: the headline comparison (Section  REF ), its robustness (Section  REF ), what drives it (Section  REF ), stability, drift and secondary metrics (Section  REF ) and scalability and cost (Section  REF ); Section  REF discusses them and Section  REF concludes.

Choosing the reported comparison after inspecting the test results is itself a recognised source of optimism: Cawley and Talbot quantify the selection bias in performance evaluation that follows model selection, Jelizarow et al.  illustrate over-optimism in method comparisons, and Berk et al.  and Taylor and Tibshirani formalise valid inference after selection; Section  REF treats the headline comparisons of this paper in that light.

Jeong et al.  formalised LLM feature selection from names and task descriptions and found GPT-4 selections competitive with LASSO without access to training rows, Li et al.  contrasted text-based and data-driven modes, and Zhang et al.  used LLM priors to set LASSO penalties; all are evaluated on general tabular benchmarks with random splits.

Selection must satisfy four partly conflicting requirements: relevance established on development data only; limited redundancy, which inflates variance in logistic regression and complicates attribution; reproducibility, because a subset that changes at every refit is hard to govern and explain to a validator; and decision-time availability with a distribution stable enough to be monitored with PSI .

Scale adds a fifth requirement: on a universe of a thousand or more features observed on a million decisions, relevance statistics, and for redundancy-based selectors pairwise redundancy statistics, are recomputed in every fold, so a pre-screening stage that reduces the candidate pool can lower the cost of the downstream selectors.

The information value (IV) of scorecard practice bins a feature and compares the shares MATH and MATH of non-events and events in bin MATH through the weight of evidence (WOE) , Mutual information MATH is the general-purpose relevance statistic, and mRMR adds greedily the feature that maximises relevance minus its average redundancy with the already selected set MATH , with mutual information estimated by nearest-neighbour estimators : the estimator of Kraskov et al. between continuous variables and that of Ross between a continuous feature and the binary target.

Formally, let MATH be the engineered universe of MATH original features, MATH and MATH the development population and the held-out population, labelled HO throughout because it is a later calendar period only for LendingClub and Stability 2024 and a recency-based covariate-shift holdout for Home Credit (Section  REF ), and MATH a fixed budget.

A selector is a map MATH from development data to a subset MATH with MATH , and it is judged on three quantities: the held-out discrimination MATH of a fixed model class MATH fitted on MATH using MATH only; the reproducibility of MATH across development folds, measured by the Nogueira statistic MATH and mean pairwise Jaccard similarity; and the drift of the selected features between MATH and MATH , measured by PSI.

Semantic selection instead uses what a feature is: names, descriptions, source lineage, aggregation depth and logical type carry the information an experienced analyst uses when reviewing a variable book, and this first-pass review, a pre-screen of the universe that consumes no data rows, is the task delegated to the language model .

The ranking is a cached artefact that is target-free itself, although a pipeline containing it is target-aware whenever screening or refinement uses labels, and, where it was requested separately for each fold (Home Credit and LendingClub), its fold-to-fold agreement is reported with the Nogueira statistic and pairwise Jaccard similarity (Section  REF ).

It is measured here by mean pairwise Jaccard similarity and by the chance-corrected estimator of Nogueira et al. , which generalises Kuncheva's correction to a universe of size MATH ; both are defined in Section  REF , and the choice of MATH matters because the chance correction grows as the universe shrinks, so values computed over different universes are not directly comparable.

The engineered universe is assembled (529 predictors for Home Credit, 675 for LendingClub, 1,959 for Stability 2024) and the event definition of Section  REF applied; for Stability 2024 a prediction-time availability review of 461 source variables approved 434 raw predictors, and on LendingClub the same kind of review removed every post-origination field and the platform's own pricing and grading fields before the 675 features were built from roughly 93 source columns (Section  REF ).

Each dataset is split along its ordering index, calendar time for LendingClub and Stability 2024 and prior-application recency for Home Credit, into a development population (DEV) and a held-out population (HO), and DEV is divided into five expanding-window folds along the same index, with one index unit omitted between training and validation partitions (same-date decisions stay together in Stability 2024).

Every selector, classical and LLM-assisted, works from the same candidate set: the features of the engineered universe with at most 90% missing values on the training partition of the earliest fold, a screen computed once per dataset, held fixed across the folds and using no outcomes.

The information-value interval of MATH is used within the IV/WOE ranker and as the screening stage of IV then Boruta; the upper bound, the conventional leakage warning of scorecard practice, removed nothing, because no feature of any of the three universes reaches an information value of 0.50 on the earliest training partition.

The thirteen strategies of Sections  REF – REF (Table  REF ), and the classical voting family of REF , produce a subset of MATH (logistic regression) or MATH (CatBoost) original features; target-free rankings use no outcome; the semantic ranking is requested separately for each fold partition on Home Credit and LendingClub, and one ranking served every fold on Stability 2024 (Section  REF ); target-aware selectors are fitted per fold.

Everything is refitted on full DEV; rankings, subsets and settings are recorded in a hash-bound manifest; the frozen pipeline then scores the HO population, and no retuning of that pipeline follows within the protocol version (changes between versions are summarised in Section  REF and recorded in REF , Table  REF ).

The order of operations is fixed: eligibility screening and selection operate on original features, one column per candidate, so a categorical variable is selected or rejected as a whole, and one-hot expansion is performed only after the subset has been selected, so that the budget MATH counts original variables.

IV/WOE ranks by Eq.  REF computed on the training partition with ten quantile bins , and the same statistic defines the pre-screen of IV then Boruta. mRMR applies Eq.  REF with mutual information estimated on the training partition ; its pool is the whole candidate set when it is used alone and the shortlist when it follows a semantic stage.

Domain rules is a deterministic credit-domain scorer that reads no data and calls no model: 42 named-variable rules, family and string-pattern rules for bureau, instalment, credit-card and previous-application aggregates, 15 property-attribute rules and nine semantic-group fallbacks assign each feature a priority, which aggregation suffixes and leakage status adjust, with deterministic tie ordering.

Family-capped classical re-runs the HO-rule classical leader of each case with a cap of at most MATH features per source family, where MATH is the number of source families in the dataset's universe (6 on Home Credit, 17 on LendingClub and 12 on Stability 2024), the subset filled in the base selector's own ranking order; the caps are therefore 4 and 7, 2 and 3, and 2 and 4 at MATH and MATH .

The template carries an evidence-mode placeholder with two admissible values, definitions_only and training_metadata; every call in this study used definitions_only, under which the model may use feature names, definitions, source lineage, aggregation operations and observation windows and no numerical summary of any kind, so missingness, moments, quantiles and cardinalities are withheld as well as every target-conditioned statistic, and the prompt forbids drawing on remembered dataset-specific results.

For Home Credit the definition of every source variable is the entry of the data dictionary distributed with the competition data, so no analyst phrasing enters the base definitions; for LendingClub the definitions of the source columns were written by the first author from the platform's column documentation, and every derived feature (ratio, flag, binned version, interaction, missing indicator) is described by a template from the definitions of its source columns; for Stability 2024 the first author wrote the definitions of the approved raw predictors from the provider's documentation.

In all three datasets the description of an engineered feature is the base definition with a clause for the aggregation operation and window appended from the lineage by the feature-engineering code, so that, for example, a sum over eleven months is described as the total over eleven months; the template is applied to every feature in the same way and no feature-specific phrasing is added or edited afterwards.

On Home Credit the candidate list is the same 373 of the 529 features in every call, fixed by the missingness screen on the earliest training fold; on LendingClub it is all 675 features, none of which fails the screen; on Stability 2024 it is the 1,068 eligible features (Table  REF ).

On Home Credit six rankings of 100 names were obtained, one per partition, and the budgets of 20, 40, 60 and 100 are their prefixes; on LendingClub a separate call was made for each budget of 20, 40, 60 and 100 names, giving 24 cached rankings; on Stability 2024 one ranking of 100 names was obtained in a single call, accepted at the first attempt.

Each response is validated as above, cached and hash-bound, and the cached response rather than a fresh call is the reproducible artefact: the cached orderings all differ from one another, and calls with identical prompt, model and temperature returned different lists, so a fixed model identifier and zero temperature do not guarantee identical outputs (Section  REF ).

The released universes contain demographic fields that fair-lending rules treat as protected attributes in many jurisdictions: applicant gender and family status on Home Credit (CODE_GENDER, NAME_FAMILY_STATUS) and the sex field of the person table on Stability 2024; age fields appear as well, and their treatment differs across regimes.

An exclusion applied in the prompt alone would have narrowed the pool for the LLM-assisted family while the classical selectors kept drawing from the full candidate set, so the two families would no longer have been compared on the same universe; and any change to the prompt invalidates the cached rankings on which every reported LLM-assisted result rests.

Where a lender's policy excludes protected attributes, the exclusion belongs in the eligibility screen, where it binds every selector; that screen was not applied in this study, which does not evaluate fairness (Section  REF ), and Section  REF records where these fields appear in the headline subsets.

To test whether the ranking depends on recognising feature names, the six Home Credit calls were repeated in two obfuscated arms with everything except the feature records held fixed: the same snapshot ( URL ), temperature 0, JSON response format, the template of REF , the definition-only evidence mode, the same 373 candidates per partition and the same strict validation.

In arm A every name was replaced by an identifier F001–F529 drawn from a seeded permutation (seed 20260914) of the universe, the permutation being drawn per partition so that no identifier carries meaning across calls, and every literal occurrence of the original name was removed from the description text as well; the model saw only identifiers and descriptions, and the identifier-to-name table never entered a prompt.

Each arm yields six rankings of 100 identifiers, decoded and carried through the frozen downstream pipeline exactly as the named rankings are: top 20 to logistic regression and top 40 to CatBoost, five fold models plus the full-DEV refit with the fixed configurations of Section  REF (seed 42), scored on the same 120,053 HO rows.

To test whether the results depend on how the descriptions are phrased, every description in the three candidate sets was rebuilt from lineage alone by a fixed template stating the raw table, raw variable, depth, aggregation operation, window and type rule of the feature, with no statement of credit meaning; the name, source family, lineage formula and semantic group of each record were unchanged.

The ranking calls were repeated under the call structure, template, snapshot, temperature, evidence mode, candidate sets and validation of the cached rankings, and the new rankings were carried through the frozen downstream pipelines to the same HO observations: pure LLM in all six cases, and the LLM-assisted leader of the two cases in which it is not pure LLM, stable core plus LLM fill on Home Credit with logistic regression and LLM then mRMR on LendingClub v2 with CatBoost.

Features selected in at least four of the five resamples form the stable core, ordered by selection frequency and mean rank; the subset is then completed from the LLM ranking in rank order, without padding from unranked features, so that the core preserves reproducibility while semantically prioritised variables fill the remaining budget.

Across versions the comparator set changed from a single mRMR baseline to the classical family leader of each case; the feature descriptions supplied to the language model were revised (their preparation is described in Section  REF ); mutual-information mRMR replaced the RF/correlation filter as the stand-alone statistical selector; fold-level rank tests gave way to paired bootstrap intervals without significance claims, the development rule being specified after the HO-rule results were known; and the Stability 2024 cutoff was moved once, from 2020-02-26 to 2020-02-01 (Section  REF ).

The 675 features were generated deterministically from roughly 93 distinct columns of the loan book, and every one of them is an attribute of a single loan and its applicant at origination: 116 raw columns carried through unchanged, 180 binary flags, 158 ratios, 88 missing indicators, 78 further engineered variables, 27 binned versions, 19 interactions and 9 categoricals.

No feature aggregates across loans or over calendar periods, and the only elapsed-time quantity is the age of the credit file at issue, the number of months between issue_ d and earliest_ cr_ line, which is an attribute of the loan rather than a time index.

The second is LendingClub's own pricing and grading fields, int_ rate, grade, sub_ grade, installment and funded_ amnt, which encode the platform's own assessment of the application: excluding them poses the selection problem over applicant and bureau attributes rather than over a re-encoding of a credit decision already taken, at the cost that the AUC levels reported here are not comparable with LendingClub studies that retain the platform's grade or interest rate.

Several credit-file attributes of the loan book were introduced by the platform during the sample period, so their missingness is higher in DEV than in HO, and the features derived from them inherit that pattern; the highest missingness rate reached by any LendingClub feature on the earliest training partition is 82%, so the screen that defines the candidate set retains all 675; 566 features fall below 40%, two lie between 40 and 60% and 107 between 60 and 82%.

None of them appears anywhere in the cached semantic rankings, so no LLM-assisted subset contains one; the target-aware selectors compute their criteria on the DEV training partition, where a field that is sparse in that period carries little information value, mutual information or model importance and is down-weighted by construction.

Thirty-six-month loans account for 445,596 of the 598,649 DEV loans and 232,361 of the 293,105 HO loans, with event rates of 14.5% (36-month) and 34.3% (60-month) in DEV and 19.8% and 36.4% in HO, so the DEV–HO difference in event rate arises within both terms and not only from a change in term mix.

At depth 1 ten table families with several rows per case, applprev_ 1, tax_ registry_ a_ 1, tax_ registry_ b_ 1, tax_ registry_ c_ 1, credit_ bureau_ a_ 1, credit_ bureau_ b_ 1, other_ 1, person_ 1, deposit_ 1 and debitcard_ 1, are reduced to one row per case with fixed outcome-independent operations: count, mean, minimum, maximum, standard deviation and the chronologically latest value for numeric and date variables, and mode, most recent category and number of distinct values for categorical variables.

For LendingClub and Stability 2024 the index is calendar time and HO is later than DEV, which addresses whether a selected subset and a fitted model still rank risk correctly on loans issued or decisions taken after development; random splits would mask both population drift and the optimism of subsets tuned on the same period .

The split orders decisions, not outcomes: the provider-defined outcome horizons are not fully specified (Section  REF ), so the design is a chronological holdout and does not by itself establish that every development label would have been observable at the held-out decision dates, as a fully simulated deployment would require.

The event rate differs between the two windows, 7.93% in DEV against 8.90% in HO (Table  REF ), so the Home Credit holdout asks the frozen pipelines to rank risk in a subgroup that is both differently distributed and riskier than the development population, a harder target than a shift in covariates alone.

The split point was fixed on the index rather than on a target share of the population, so the Home Credit HO population (120,053 applications drawn from a 240-day recency window) is larger than DEV (99,092 from a 360-day window): applicants whose most recent previous application is recent are denser in the release than those whose most recent one is old.

Within DEV, five expanding-window folds are formed along the same index, each training partition consisting of the lowest-index observations and the validation partition of a later block, with one index unit, one index day for Home Credit and LendingClub and one decision date for Stability 2024, assigned to neither partition.

This omitted unit is not a calendar embargo: LendingClub is indexed by issue month, so on that dataset it separates the partitions by position in the ordering and not by elapsed time, and it is the ordered split itself that keeps later loans out of training.

This restriction can preferentially retain early defaults and early repayments when other loans of the same cohort remain unresolved, and follow-up duration differs across issue cohorts and between 36- and 60-month terms, so population composition and the reported DEV–HO event-rate difference (Table  REF ) should be read with this selection in mind, and the LendingClub findings describe this resolved-loan population.

CatBoost uses depth 10, learning rate 0.01, L2 leaf regularisation 95, minimum 290 observations per leaf, a feature-sampling rate (rsm) of 0.90, random strength 0.125, depthwise growth, Bernoulli bootstrap with subsample 0.55, the Logloss objective with AUC evaluation, balanced class weights, seed 42, four threads and a fixed 1,500 iterations without early stopping, so that no validation information enters the fitted model.

The same two configurations are applied to every feature count, from the 20- and 40-feature subsets to the full-feature reference models on 373, 675 and 1,959 features, the Stability 2024 references being fitted on the unscreened 1,959-feature universe; the CatBoost configuration was carried over unchanged from the authors' prior credit-scoring work at the Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan on a separate, non-public portfolio, where it had been tuned on a validation set, and the logistic-regression configuration is a standard L2-penalised setting with MATH .

Larger linear subsets improved development discrimination only marginally, on average MATH development AUC at MATH and MATH at MATH for one and a half to two times the feature count, so MATH was fixed as the compact operating point; CatBoost continued to benefit up to MATH , gained nothing further beyond it on average, and was less sensitive to redundant predictors.

MATH is reported for selectors refitted in each fold and, over the same candidate set, for the pure LLM lists, which were requested separately per fold rather than refitted; because the candidate list supplied is the same in every call (Section  REF ), a fold-to-fold difference between those lists reflects the sampling of the language model at a fixed prompt rather than any change in what it was asked to rank.

Because the holdout plays no part in choosing what is compared, this set is free of the selection effect of the first; it is nevertheless reported in the same form, as effect sizes with intervals and without a test, for the reason given at the end of this section.

In both sets the two pipelines are scored on identical HO observations paired by observation identifier (SK_ ID_ CURR for Home Credit, a stable identifier derived from the processed source row for LendingClub, the decision identifier for Stability 2024), and the paired HO ROC-AUC difference, LLM-assisted minus classical, is reported with a 95% interval from 2,000 target-stratified paired bootstrap resamples that draw the same observation indices for both pipelines with seed 20260721.

The interval describes the sampling variability of the difference between the two compared pipelines on the HO population; in the descriptive set it does not account for the selection of those pipelines, and in neither set does it account for the sampling of the language model at a fixed prompt, because the resampling draws HO observations while the cached semantic ranking, and therefore the selected subset of the LLM-assisted pipeline, is held fixed in every resample.

Because large HO samples make small differences detectable, effect sizes are always reported with the intervals , and a paired AUC difference of at least MATH , two Gini points, is treated as material; smaller differences are reported but are not counted as a result in either direction.

A paired DeLong test, like the paired bootstrap, treats the two fitted pipelines as fixed and asks how the AUC difference would vary if the HO observations were resampled; with 120,053 to 369,147 paired observations that question is answered to the fourth decimal and every headline difference would be significant at any conventional level, so the test would report the size of the holdout rather than anything about the methods.

The variation that bears on the claim of this paper lies elsewhere: across portfolios, of which there are three from at most two independent lenders (Section  REF ); across prompts, of which there is one; across responses of the language model, of which there is one per case, ten on Stability 2024 (Section  REF ); and across seeds, of which there is one.

In each dataset–backbone case the LLM-assisted and the classical family leader, the selector with the highest observed HO AUC in its family, are compared on identical HO observations; both leaders were chosen on the HO results, so the comparison is descriptive (Section  REF ); the development-rule comparison follows below.

The LLM-assisted leader is pure LLM in four cases (Home Credit CatBoost, LendingClub v2 LR, Stability 2024 LR and Stability 2024 CatBoost), LLM then mRMR in one (LendingClub v2 CatBoost) and stable core plus LLM fill in the remaining case, Home Credit LR, where the classical selector leads.

The pattern does not depend on comparing family leaders: excluding the three selectors declared as floors (domain rules, Random  MATH and PCA), the mean HO AUC of the remaining six classical selectors is below the mean of the four LLM-assisted pipelines in the same five cases, by MATH to MATH (Table  REF ), and above it on Home Credit logistic regression, by MATH .

An L1-penalised selector run afterwards, CatBoost's native categorical handling, the LendingClub resolution filter and the source concentration of the subsets are examined as robustness checks in Section  REF , and the input width each headline subset delivers to its model, which MATH does not fix, is reported in REF (Table  REF ).

Choosing each family's leader on the development folds instead (Table  REF ) changes the compared pair in five of six cases but not the outcome: the LLM-assisted leader is higher in the same five cases, by MATH to MATH , and the classical leader keeps Home Credit logistic regression by MATH .

The rule makes IV then Boruta the classical leader on both Home Credit cases and RFE CatBoost on both LendingClub v2 cases and on Stability 2024 CatBoost, and LLM then mRMR the LLM-assisted leader on Home Credit logistic regression; only Stability 2024 logistic regression keeps its pair, pure LLM against RFE CatBoost, and with it its difference, and five of the six margins are wider than under the HO rule.

The DEV-chosen classical leader is the HO-best classical selector only on Stability 2024 logistic regression and sits below it by MATH to MATH in the other five cases, whereas the DEV-chosen LLM-assisted leader is the HO-best one in five cases and below it by MATH on Home Credit logistic regression.

The smaller development-to-holdout change of the LLM-assisted subsets is a finding in its own right, consistent with their lower selected-feature drift (Table  REF ), and it means that the agreement between the two leader rules is partly a consequence of that finding rather than an independent corroboration of it.

The column "Full" is the HO AUC of the untuned full-feature reference, fitted on every candidate feature (on Stability 2024, the unscreened 1,959) under the same fixed configuration; it is context only and supports no claim about compact subsets against the full feature set (Section  REF ).

On Home Credit, CODE_GENDER holds rank 3 in the mRMR logistic-regression subset, rank 14 in the RFE CatBoost subset and rank 10 in the pure LLM CatBoost subset, and NAME_FAMILY_STATUS holds rank 9 in the pure LLM CatBoost subset and rank 39 in the RFE CatBoost subset; on Stability 2024 the two aggregates of the person-table sex field occupy ranks 1 and 6 of the CatBoost SHAP subset and no LLM-assisted subset contains one; the LendingClub v2 headline subsets contain no such field.

On Stability 2024 the four LLM-assisted pipelines lie within MATH of one another with logistic regression and within MATH with CatBoost, pure LLM leading under both backbones (Table  REF ); resolved by month of decision, pure LLM has the higher AUC in every one of the nine months of the held-out window under both backbones ( REF ).

The reading is the first of the three fixed before the run: the AUC holds without the names while the lists partly overlap, so the value of the ranking rests on the definitions, and the familiar names shaped the top of the named lists without carrying their predictive value.

Obfuscating a name leaves a definition that may itself be recognisable, so the ablation weakens the name channel rather than removing it; and the comparison is descriptive, the differences of arm A being smaller than the fold-to-fold spread of a single arm, and covers Home Credit only, the dataset on which the exposure is largest (Section  REF ).

Whether a rule concentrating on the same tables would do as well is tested by the two diversity controls of Section  REF : capping the classical leader per source family lowers it in all six cases and leaves it below the LLM-assisted leader in five, and confining it to the two static tables on Stability 2024 leaves it MATH and MATH below pure LLM over the same pool (Table  REF ; REF ).

The pure LLM lists were requested separately per fold partition rather than refitted, and Table  REF reports their fold agreement over the candidate set on Home Credit and LendingClub, where five fold lists exist per case; the cached rankings all differ, the six of 100 names on Home Credit and all 24 on LendingClub.

The ordering holds pair by pair: on Home Credit and LendingClub the least similar fold pair of the most reproducible classical selector is at least as similar as the most similar pair of the pure LLM list of the same case (Min and Max columns of Table  REF ), so the difference between the two families does not rest on a single fold split.

On Stability 2024 one ranking served every fold, so its fold agreement is 1 by construction and is not reported; in its place the sampling of the model at a fixed prompt was isolated directly by repeating the full-DEV call ten times with the same prompt, snapshot, temperature 0 and the same 1,068 candidate records.

Over that candidate set the ten lists reach Nogueira 0.8052 at MATH and 0.7766 at MATH (Table  REF ), level with the most reproducible classical selector of the same case over the same universe (0.7860 and 0.7793); the mean pairwise Jaccard of the ten lists at MATH , 0.6908, exceeds that selector's fold mean of 0.6666 and lies inside its fold-pair range (Table  REF ).

The pure LLM rows of Table  REF for Home Credit and LendingClub measure the same quantity, the candidate list being fixed there too (Section  REF ), and are much lower; because the chance correction depends on MATH (Section  REF ) the three are not on a common scale and the comparison between datasets is not made here.

Carrying each response through the frozen downstream pipeline gives the held-out AUC ranges, medians and standard deviations of Table  REF ; the cached values of Table  REF lie above four and above seven of the ten repeats, inside the body of the distribution rather than at its top.

The margin over the classical leader stays positive in all twenty refits (Table  REF ), so no repeat reverses the direction of the comparison; two of the ten logistic-regression repeats fall below the materiality bar of 0.010 (Section  REF ), by 0.0014 and 0.0003, while every CatBoost repeat clears it.

The same quantity was measured on Home Credit and LendingClub, where five semantic rankings per dataset were cached, one per fold partition, over the identical candidate list; each ranking's top MATH was carried through the frozen full-DEV pipeline and scored once on HO, twenty refits in all.

Its fold pairs reach the classical range: in all six cases its most similar pair is at or above the least similar pair of the most reproducible classical selector (Min and Max columns of Table  REF ), so the construction recovers classical-level agreement on part of the fold pairs.

On Home Credit and LendingClub it is level with the pure LLM lists it refits on, within 0.04 in three of the four cases and 0.11 below on Home Credit logistic regression; on Stability 2024, where one semantic ranking served every fold, its 0.49 (logistic regression) and 0.55 (CatBoost) are produced by the Boruta refit alone.

The LLM-assisted leader has the lower mean drift than the classical leader of the same case in five of the six cases and the lower median in all six (Table  REF ); the exception is Stability 2024 logistic regression, where pure LLM's mean exceeds RFE CatBoost's (0.0174 against 0.0092).

Every one of the twelve means sits an order of magnitude below the conventional action threshold of 0.10, so the selected subsets of both families would pass a drift review unchanged; the comparison between the families therefore reports a measurable difference in the composition of the subsets, consistent with the prompt's instruction to favour durable inputs, and not an operational advantage in drift.

The largest single-feature drift in a headline subset is 0.114, a tax-registry row count in the CatBoost SHAP subset on Stability 2024, followed by 0.086 for a count of instalments without delinquency in the pure LLM subset of the same case and 0.058 for an instalment-timing variance in the RFE CatBoost subset on Home Credit; on Home Credit, where the held-out population is shifted in prior-application recency, the most drifted selected feature of every leader is a bureau, instalment or credit-card field rather than a previous-application recency field.

One downstream saving from a reduced candidate pool was measured under matched conditions: on Stability 2024 fold 1, on the same machine, the mRMR stage took 522 seconds over the unscreened 1,959-feature universe and 21 seconds over a 100-feature pool, a factor of 25 for a pool twenty times smaller.

A pool of that size is what the semantic stage hands to the statistical stage of LLM then mRMR under CatBoost (Section  REF ), and that stage reads the variable book and no data rows, so its own cost depends on the number of candidate records and not on the number of decisions.

The 30 calls consumed 806,757 input and 56,495 output tokens, for a direct API cost between USD 0.171 and USD 0.413 at the GPT-4.1 mini list prices of USD 0.40 per million input tokens, 0.10 per million cached input tokens and 1.60 per million output tokens; the bounds correspond to all input charged at the cached rate and at the uncached rate.

The saved runs of the final protocol were executed on the CPU of one machine with 16 logical (10 physical) cores and 39.6 GiB of RAM, with four estimator threads and no accelerator; peak process memory was 7.4 to 10.7 GB for the Home Credit selectors and full-feature references, 19.1 to 29.0 GB for their LendingClub counterparts and 27.0 to 29.0 GB for their Stability 2024 counterparts.

The answer is conditional: in five of six dataset–backbone cases the LLM-assisted family leader exceeds the classical family leader, whether the leaders are chosen on the HO results, in which case the comparison is descriptive, on the development folds, or under the most adversarial pairing of the two (Section  REF , Table  REF ); on Home Credit logistic regression the classical leader is higher under all three rules, mutual-information mRMR by 0.021 and 0.027 and IV then Boruta by 0.010.

Within these comparisons the semantic ranking therefore most often had the higher HO AUC when used directly; statistical refinement of the semantic pool led in one case, and on Home Credit CatBoost the refined pipeline (LLM then mRMR) had a lower held-out AUC than pure LLM (Table  REF ).

The choice between them for a deployed pipeline is a development-stage decision, to be made on development data rather than on the holdout used to report final performance, which is how the leaders of Table  REF were identified and why Table  REF repeats the comparison with leaders chosen on development data.

The pure LLM lists of the discrimination-leading pipelines differ from fold to fold, Nogueira 0.41 to 0.63 over the same candidate set (Section  REF ), and the best-discriminating selector in this study is, with LLM then Boruta, the least reproducible one in Table  REF , and its reported AUC is that of the particular cached responses.

Ten repeated calls on the Stability 2024 partition bound how much that last point costs there: the ranking varies (Table  REF ) but the held-out AUC moves by 0.0095 and 0.0092, inside the materiality bar, and the direction of the comparison holds in every repeat (Section  REF ).

A diversity control separates that result from source concentration: a classical selector confined to the two static tables the semantic ranking drew from on Stability 2024 stays MATH and MATH below pure LLM over the same pool, and a per-family cap leaves the classical leader below its LLM-assisted counterpart in five of the six cases (Table  REF ), so the margins are not reproduced by concentrating on the same tables.

On Home Credit, the dataset whose variable book is most widely documented, replacing every name by a seeded identifier leaves the held-out AUC of the pure LLM pipeline within 0.005 of the named result under both backbones, while removing the definitions and keeping the names costs about 0.03.

Its twelve comparisons, three pool sizes in each of the four Home Credit and LendingClub cases, were fixed in a protocol file before any held-out result of the family was computed, and every one is positive, from MATH to MATH AUC, with paired bootstrap intervals that exclude zero and Holm-adjusted paired DeLong tests significant within each family (Table  REF ).

The LLM-assisted pipeline that leads discrimination on LendingClub rests on cached per-fold rankings whose fold agreement is among the lowest in Table  REF : calls with identical prompt, model and temperature returned different orderings, and the pure LLM lists reach Nogueira 0.41 to 0.63 over the same candidate set on which the most reproducible classical selectors reach at least 0.78 (Table  REF ), with LLM then Boruta no more reproducible than the lists it refits on (Section  REF ).

It moves held-out AUC by 0.0095 and 0.0092, both inside the materiality bar of Section  REF , with the direction of the comparison unchanged in all twenty refits (Section  REF ); on that dataset caching the response therefore fixes a choice that was not, in the event, a material one.

The stable-core construction is the device intended to raise the reproducibility of a semantically screened subset; the stable-core hybrid is the LLM-assisted family leader on Home Credit logistic regression, although it remains below mRMR there, and its fold stability, 0.08 to 0.28 above pure LLM in Nogueira, is reported in Table  REF .

Feature drift within the selected subsets is low for all twelve headline pipelines, mean selected-feature PSI of 0.0024 to 0.0189, and the LLM-assisted leader drifts less than the classical leader of the same case by mean in five of six cases and by median in all six (Table  REF , Section  REF ), which is reported because it is the one measured indication that the prompt's instruction to favour temporally durable inputs shaped the selection.

The domain-rules baseline transfers least: its rule set is written around the Home Credit variable book (Section  REF ), and on LendingClub with logistic regression it reaches 0.5525, below the 0.6038 of a random subset of the same size, so it should be read as a portfolio-specific expert scorer rather than as a generic domain baseline.

Resolving the comparison by month ( REF ) shows that the ordering of the two families is the same in all nine months under both backbones, so the direction of the result does not rest on the composition of any one period; portfolio-specific interventions remain a possible influence on the reported magnitudes, which are not established as robust to a regime shift.

The semantic stage is paid once per variable book: it reads one record per candidate and no data rows, so its cost depends on the size of the variable book and not on the number of decisions, and its cached response is reused at every refit.

Home Credit is ordered by the recency of the applicant's most recent previous application rather than by calendar time, so its held-out population is a recency-based covariate-shift holdout of applicants with a qualifying previous application, and its results do not extend to applicants without one; the two windows together cover 219,145 of the 307,511 applications in the training release, and the remaining 28.7 per cent, applicants whose most recent previous application lies outside day MATH to MATH or who have none, are not used.

The design tests transfer to that recency-defined subgroup, whose event rate is higher than the development population's; it does not establish that the relation between features and outcome is unchanged across the split, which covariate shift in the strict sense would require and which no split of observational data can verify.

The development-rule comparison chooses the leaders on the development folds, but its rule was specified after the HO-rule results were known, and neither set accounts for the earlier protocol versions that inspected held-out results; the final evaluation is a frozen scoring run on held-out populations inspected earlier in the study.

Two backbones with one fixed configuration each are used, not tuned per selector, with balanced class weights and no recalibration, so probability metrics compare selectors within a dataset only, and the ordering among selectors is a statement about that configuration rather than about each selector at its own best setting.

On LendingClub the variables that public kernels and competition write-ups headline, the platform's own interest rate, grade and sub-grade, are not in the universe at all (Section  REF ), so what the model ranks there are applicant and bureau attributes whose credit meaning an analyst would recognise without having seen this dataset; the largest LLM-assisted margins in the study are obtained on that universe.

The concern bears most directly on Home Credit, whose feature names and their standing in published solutions are widely documented, and the ablation of Section  REF tests it there: with the names withheld the held-out AUC is unchanged and the recall-driven ordering of the external scores disappears, whereas withholding the definitions costs about 0.03 AUC.

The pure LLM rows of Table  REF isolate the sampling of the model at a fixed prompt, the candidate list being the same in every call (Section  REF ); Stability 2024 has no pure LLM row because its single ranking served every fold, and the ten repeated calls reported in Section  REF measure the same quantity there directly.

With HO populations of 120,000 to 369,000 observations small AUC differences are statistically detectable, so effect sizes matter more than any test; formal inference is confined to the pre-declared classical voting family of REF , and the headline comparisons of Tables  REF and REF are reported as effect sizes with intervals and no test (Section  REF ).

In particular, protected attributes were eligible for every selector and appear in headline subsets of both families (Sections  REF and REF ); a deployed contract would exclude them at the eligibility screen, and how the language model ranks the remaining candidates under such an exclusion was not measured.

This paper asked whether semantic pre-screening, by a large language model that reads the variable book but no outcome, can select compact, competitive and governable feature subsets for credit scoring with large engineered universes, and how such subsets compare with classical selection on held-out populations later in time or shifted in applicant recency.

Across three credit portfolios and two backbones, with fixed budgets of 20 and 40 original features and each pipeline frozen before its final held-out scoring run, the LLM-assisted family leader exceeded the classical family leader in five of six cases, with paired differences of MATH to MATH under the held-out rule.

Under the development rule the differences were MATH to MATH , and the result holds whether the leaders are chosen on the held-out results, where the differences are descriptive, on the development folds, or under the most adversarial pairing of the two rules, which reproduces the held-out-rule margins, and the LLM-assisted subsets lost less AUC from development to holdout than the classical ones.

Reproducibility and drift were reported as separate outcomes: refitted classical selectors were the most reproducible, whereas the pure LLM lists that led discrimination differed from call to call and were, with LLM then Boruta, the least reproducible selectors in the table, so the best-discriminating selector was among the least reproducible.

The pre-screening stage should be governed by an explicit information contract, a cached ranking and the same freeze, drift and stability monitoring applied to any other selector, and the contract must carry the lender's protected-attribute policy, because the expert persona of the prompt did not supply one (Section  REF ).

For research, the results argue for reporting discrimination, subset reproducibility and drift separately, and for held-out evaluation on populations that are scored once and never used to revise the protocol, temporal where the data allow it, whenever feature selection is compared; this study did not achieve that standard, and reports the fact.

Extending the evaluation to additional lenders, to repeated LLM runs on the two portfolios where only cached per-fold lists exist, to a second language model and to the metadata evidence mode the prompt already admits, and to profit- and fairness-aware objectives are natural next steps; the second language model and the metadata mode would separate what is specific to this model snapshot and to the definition-only contract from what the semantic pre-screen contributes in general.

sentences_over_60.text: Supervised selectors are refitted in every validation fold and at every model refresh, and their cost grows with the number of decisions and, for redundancy-aware selectors, with the number of candidates over which redundancy is computed: on the first development fold of Stability 2024, one mRMR pass took 522 seconds over the 1,959-feature universe and 21 seconds over a 100-feature pool.

First, a held-out comparison, temporal for LendingClub and Stability 2024 and recency-shifted for Home Credit, of classical, model-based and LLM pre-screened selection, whose semantic stage reads no data rows, across three credit portfolios of up to 1,959 engineered features and 1.5 million decisions (1,526,659) and two backbones; the six paired HO comparisons between the methods with the highest observed HO AUC in each family are reported as effect sizes with paired bootstrap intervals, and repeated under two further leader-choice rules, one of which uses no held-out information to choose the compared methods.

Section  REF reviews related work, Section  REF gives background, Sections  REF and REF specify the methods and the experimental setup, and Section  REF reports the results in the order of the questions a reader is likely to ask: the headline comparison (Section  REF ), its robustness (Section  REF ), what drives it (Section  REF ), stability, drift and secondary metrics (Section  REF ) and scalability and cost (Section  REF ); Section  REF discusses them and Section  REF concludes.

Choosing the reported comparison after inspecting the test results is itself a recognised source of optimism: Cawley and Talbot quantify the selection bias in performance evaluation that follows model selection, Jelizarow et al.  illustrate over-optimism in method comparisons, and Berk et al.  and Taylor and Tibshirani formalise valid inference after selection; Section  REF treats the headline comparisons of this paper in that light.

The information value (IV) of scorecard practice bins a feature and compares the shares MATH and MATH of non-events and events in bin MATH through the weight of evidence (WOE) , Mutual information MATH is the general-purpose relevance statistic, and mRMR adds greedily the feature that maximises relevance minus its average redundancy with the already selected set MATH , with mutual information estimated by nearest-neighbour estimators : the estimator of Kraskov et al. between continuous variables and that of Ross between a continuous feature and the binary target.

A selector is a map MATH from development data to a subset MATH with MATH , and it is judged on three quantities: the held-out discrimination MATH of a fixed model class MATH fitted on MATH using MATH only; the reproducibility of MATH across development folds, measured by the Nogueira statistic MATH and mean pairwise Jaccard similarity; and the drift of the selected features between MATH and MATH , measured by PSI.

The engineered universe is assembled (529 predictors for Home Credit, 675 for LendingClub, 1,959 for Stability 2024) and the event definition of Section  REF applied; for Stability 2024 a prediction-time availability review of 461 source variables approved 434 raw predictors, and on LendingClub the same kind of review removed every post-origination field and the platform's own pricing and grading fields before the 675 features were built from roughly 93 source columns (Section  REF ).

The thirteen strategies of Sections  REF – REF (Table  REF ), and the classical voting family of REF , produce a subset of MATH (logistic regression) or MATH (CatBoost) original features; target-free rankings use no outcome; the semantic ranking is requested separately for each fold partition on Home Credit and LendingClub, and one ranking served every fold on Stability 2024 (Section  REF ); target-aware selectors are fitted per fold.

Family-capped classical re-runs the HO-rule classical leader of each case with a cap of at most MATH features per source family, where MATH is the number of source families in the dataset's universe (6 on Home Credit, 17 on LendingClub and 12 on Stability 2024), the subset filled in the base selector's own ranking order; the caps are therefore 4 and 7, 2 and 3, and 2 and 4 at MATH and MATH .

The template carries an evidence-mode placeholder with two admissible values, definitions_only and training_metadata; every call in this study used definitions_only, under which the model may use feature names, definitions, source lineage, aggregation operations and observation windows and no numerical summary of any kind, so missingness, moments, quantiles and cardinalities are withheld as well as every target-conditioned statistic, and the prompt forbids drawing on remembered dataset-specific results.

For Home Credit the definition of every source variable is the entry of the data dictionary distributed with the competition data, so no analyst phrasing enters the base definitions; for LendingClub the definitions of the source columns were written by the first author from the platform's column documentation, and every derived feature (ratio, flag, binned version, interaction, missing indicator) is described by a template from the definitions of its source columns; for Stability 2024 the first author wrote the definitions of the approved raw predictors from the provider's documentation.

In all three datasets the description of an engineered feature is the base definition with a clause for the aggregation operation and window appended from the lineage by the feature-engineering code, so that, for example, a sum over eleven months is described as the total over eleven months; the template is applied to every feature in the same way and no feature-specific phrasing is added or edited afterwards.

On Home Credit six rankings of 100 names were obtained, one per partition, and the budgets of 20, 40, 60 and 100 are their prefixes; on LendingClub a separate call was made for each budget of 20, 40, 60 and 100 names, giving 24 cached rankings; on Stability 2024 one ranking of 100 names was obtained in a single call, accepted at the first attempt.

In arm A every name was replaced by an identifier F001–F529 drawn from a seeded permutation (seed 20260914) of the universe, the permutation being drawn per partition so that no identifier carries meaning across calls, and every literal occurrence of the original name was removed from the description text as well; the model saw only identifiers and descriptions, and the identifier-to-name table never entered a prompt.

To test whether the results depend on how the descriptions are phrased, every description in the three candidate sets was rebuilt from lineage alone by a fixed template stating the raw table, raw variable, depth, aggregation operation, window and type rule of the feature, with no statement of credit meaning; the name, source family, lineage formula and semantic group of each record were unchanged.

The ranking calls were repeated under the call structure, template, snapshot, temperature, evidence mode, candidate sets and validation of the cached rankings, and the new rankings were carried through the frozen downstream pipelines to the same HO observations: pure LLM in all six cases, and the LLM-assisted leader of the two cases in which it is not pure LLM, stable core plus LLM fill on Home Credit with logistic regression and LLM then mRMR on LendingClub v2 with CatBoost.

Across versions the comparator set changed from a single mRMR baseline to the classical family leader of each case; the feature descriptions supplied to the language model were revised (their preparation is described in Section  REF ); mutual-information mRMR replaced the RF/correlation filter as the stand-alone statistical selector; fold-level rank tests gave way to paired bootstrap intervals without significance claims, the development rule being specified after the HO-rule results were known; and the Stability 2024 cutoff was moved once, from 2020-02-26 to 2020-02-01 (Section  REF ).

The second is LendingClub's own pricing and grading fields, int_ rate, grade, sub_ grade, installment and funded_ amnt, which encode the platform's own assessment of the application: excluding them poses the selection problem over applicant and bureau attributes rather than over a re-encoding of a credit decision already taken, at the cost that the AUC levels reported here are not comparable with LendingClub studies that retain the platform's grade or interest rate.

Several credit-file attributes of the loan book were introduced by the platform during the sample period, so their missingness is higher in DEV than in HO, and the features derived from them inherit that pattern; the highest missingness rate reached by any LendingClub feature on the earliest training partition is 82%, so the screen that defines the candidate set retains all 675; 566 features fall below 40%, two lie between 40 and 60% and 107 between 60 and 82%.

At depth 1 ten table families with several rows per case, applprev_ 1, tax_ registry_ a_ 1, tax_ registry_ b_ 1, tax_ registry_ c_ 1, credit_ bureau_ a_ 1, credit_ bureau_ b_ 1, other_ 1, person_ 1, deposit_ 1 and debitcard_ 1, are reduced to one row per case with fixed outcome-independent operations: count, mean, minimum, maximum, standard deviation and the chronologically latest value for numeric and date variables, and mode, most recent category and number of distinct values for categorical variables.

The split point was fixed on the index rather than on a target share of the population, so the Home Credit HO population (120,053 applications drawn from a 240-day recency window) is larger than DEV (99,092 from a 360-day window): applicants whose most recent previous application is recent are denser in the release than those whose most recent one is old.

CatBoost uses depth 10, learning rate 0.01, L2 leaf regularisation 95, minimum 290 observations per leaf, a feature-sampling rate (rsm) of 0.90, random strength 0.125, depthwise growth, Bernoulli bootstrap with subsample 0.55, the Logloss objective with AUC evaluation, balanced class weights, seed 42, four threads and a fixed 1,500 iterations without early stopping, so that no validation information enters the fitted model.

The same two configurations are applied to every feature count, from the 20- and 40-feature subsets to the full-feature reference models on 373, 675 and 1,959 features, the Stability 2024 references being fitted on the unscreened 1,959-feature universe; the CatBoost configuration was carried over unchanged from the authors' prior credit-scoring work at the Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan on a separate, non-public portfolio, where it had been tuned on a validation set, and the logistic-regression configuration is a standard L2-penalised setting with MATH .

MATH is reported for selectors refitted in each fold and, over the same candidate set, for the pure LLM lists, which were requested separately per fold rather than refitted; because the candidate list supplied is the same in every call (Section  REF ), a fold-to-fold difference between those lists reflects the sampling of the language model at a fixed prompt rather than any change in what it was asked to rank.

In both sets the two pipelines are scored on identical HO observations paired by observation identifier (SK_ ID_ CURR for Home Credit, a stable identifier derived from the processed source row for LendingClub, the decision identifier for Stability 2024), and the paired HO ROC-AUC difference, LLM-assisted minus classical, is reported with a 95% interval from 2,000 target-stratified paired bootstrap resamples that draw the same observation indices for both pipelines with seed 20260721.

The interval describes the sampling variability of the difference between the two compared pipelines on the HO population; in the descriptive set it does not account for the selection of those pipelines, and in neither set does it account for the sampling of the language model at a fixed prompt, because the resampling draws HO observations while the cached semantic ranking, and therefore the selected subset of the LLM-assisted pipeline, is held fixed in every resample.

A paired DeLong test, like the paired bootstrap, treats the two fitted pipelines as fixed and asks how the AUC difference would vary if the HO observations were resampled; with 120,053 to 369,147 paired observations that question is answered to the fourth decimal and every headline difference would be significant at any conventional level, so the test would report the size of the holdout rather than anything about the methods.

The variation that bears on the claim of this paper lies elsewhere: across portfolios, of which there are three from at most two independent lenders (Section  REF ); across prompts, of which there is one; across responses of the language model, of which there is one per case, ten on Stability 2024 (Section  REF ); and across seeds, of which there is one.

The pattern does not depend on comparing family leaders: excluding the three selectors declared as floors (domain rules, Random  MATH and PCA), the mean HO AUC of the remaining six classical selectors is below the mean of the four LLM-assisted pipelines in the same five cases, by MATH to MATH (Table  REF ), and above it on Home Credit logistic regression, by MATH .

The rule makes IV then Boruta the classical leader on both Home Credit cases and RFE CatBoost on both LendingClub v2 cases and on Stability 2024 CatBoost, and LLM then mRMR the LLM-assisted leader on Home Credit logistic regression; only Stability 2024 logistic regression keeps its pair, pure LLM against RFE CatBoost, and with it its difference, and five of the six margins are wider than under the HO rule.

On Home Credit, CODE_GENDER holds rank 3 in the mRMR logistic-regression subset, rank 14 in the RFE CatBoost subset and rank 10 in the pure LLM CatBoost subset, and NAME_FAMILY_STATUS holds rank 9 in the pure LLM CatBoost subset and rank 39 in the RFE CatBoost subset; on Stability 2024 the two aggregates of the person-table sex field occupy ranks 1 and 6 of the CatBoost SHAP subset and no LLM-assisted subset contains one; the LendingClub v2 headline subsets contain no such field.

Whether a rule concentrating on the same tables would do as well is tested by the two diversity controls of Section  REF : capping the classical leader per source family lowers it in all six cases and leaves it below the LLM-assisted leader in five, and confining it to the two static tables on Stability 2024 leaves it MATH and MATH below pure LLM over the same pool (Table  REF ; REF ).

The ordering holds pair by pair: on Home Credit and LendingClub the least similar fold pair of the most reproducible classical selector is at least as similar as the most similar pair of the pure LLM list of the same case (Min and Max columns of Table  REF ), so the difference between the two families does not rest on a single fold split.

Over that candidate set the ten lists reach Nogueira 0.8052 at MATH and 0.7766 at MATH (Table  REF ), level with the most reproducible classical selector of the same case over the same universe (0.7860 and 0.7793); the mean pairwise Jaccard of the ten lists at MATH , 0.6908, exceeds that selector's fold mean of 0.6666 and lies inside its fold-pair range (Table  REF ).

Every one of the twelve means sits an order of magnitude below the conventional action threshold of 0.10, so the selected subsets of both families would pass a drift review unchanged; the comparison between the families therefore reports a measurable difference in the composition of the subsets, consistent with the prompt's instruction to favour durable inputs, and not an operational advantage in drift.

The largest single-feature drift in a headline subset is 0.114, a tax-registry row count in the CatBoost SHAP subset on Stability 2024, followed by 0.086 for a count of instalments without delinquency in the pure LLM subset of the same case and 0.058 for an instalment-timing variance in the RFE CatBoost subset on Home Credit; on Home Credit, where the held-out population is shifted in prior-application recency, the most drifted selected feature of every leader is a bureau, instalment or credit-card field rather than a previous-application recency field.

The 30 calls consumed 806,757 input and 56,495 output tokens, for a direct API cost between USD 0.171 and USD 0.413 at the GPT-4.1 mini list prices of USD 0.40 per million input tokens, 0.10 per million cached input tokens and 1.60 per million output tokens; the bounds correspond to all input charged at the cached rate and at the uncached rate.

The saved runs of the final protocol were executed on the CPU of one machine with 16 logical (10 physical) cores and 39.6 GiB of RAM, with four estimator threads and no accelerator; peak process memory was 7.4 to 10.7 GB for the Home Credit selectors and full-feature references, 19.1 to 29.0 GB for their LendingClub counterparts and 27.0 to 29.0 GB for their Stability 2024 counterparts.

The answer is conditional: in five of six dataset–backbone cases the LLM-assisted family leader exceeds the classical family leader, whether the leaders are chosen on the HO results, in which case the comparison is descriptive, on the development folds, or under the most adversarial pairing of the two (Section  REF , Table  REF ); on Home Credit logistic regression the classical leader is higher under all three rules, mutual-information mRMR by 0.021 and 0.027 and IV then Boruta by 0.010.

A diversity control separates that result from source concentration: a classical selector confined to the two static tables the semantic ranking drew from on Stability 2024 stays MATH and MATH below pure LLM over the same pool, and a per-family cap leaves the classical leader below its LLM-assisted counterpart in five of the six cases (Table  REF ), so the margins are not reproduced by concentrating on the same tables.

The LLM-assisted pipeline that leads discrimination on LendingClub rests on cached per-fold rankings whose fold agreement is among the lowest in Table  REF : calls with identical prompt, model and temperature returned different orderings, and the pure LLM lists reach Nogueira 0.41 to 0.63 over the same candidate set on which the most reproducible classical selectors reach at least 0.78 (Table  REF ), with LLM then Boruta no more reproducible than the lists it refits on (Section  REF ).

Feature drift within the selected subsets is low for all twelve headline pipelines, mean selected-feature PSI of 0.0024 to 0.0189, and the LLM-assisted leader drifts less than the classical leader of the same case by mean in five of six cases and by median in all six (Table  REF , Section  REF ), which is reported because it is the one measured indication that the prompt's instruction to favour temporally durable inputs shaped the selection.

Home Credit is ordered by the recency of the applicant's most recent previous application rather than by calendar time, so its held-out population is a recency-based covariate-shift holdout of applicants with a qualifying previous application, and its results do not extend to applicants without one; the two windows together cover 219,145 of the 307,511 applications in the training release, and the remaining 28.7 per cent, applicants whose most recent previous application lies outside day MATH to MATH or who have none, are not used.

On LendingClub the variables that public kernels and competition write-ups headline, the platform's own interest rate, grade and sub-grade, are not in the universe at all (Section  REF ), so what the model ranks there are applicant and bureau attributes whose credit meaning an analyst would recognise without having seen this dataset; the largest LLM-assisted margins in the study are obtained on that universe.

Under the development rule the differences were MATH to MATH , and the result holds whether the leaders are chosen on the held-out results, where the differences are descriptive, on the development folds, or under the most adversarial pairing of the two rules, which reproduces the held-out-rule margins, and the LLM-assisted subsets lost less AUC from development to holdout than the classical ones.

Extending the evaluation to additional lenders, to repeated LLM runs on the two portfolios where only cached per-fold lists exist, to a second language model and to the metadata evidence mode the prompt already admits, and to profit- and fairness-aware objectives are natural next steps; the second language model and the metadata mode would separate what is specific to this model snapshot and to the definition-only contract from what the semantic pre-screen contributes in general.

highlights.text: An LLM pre-screens a 1,959-feature credit universe from definitions, no data rows
The semantic stage's cost depends on the variable book, not the number of decisions
LLM-assisted leaders win 5 of 6 held-out cases under three leader-choice rules
LLM-assisted subsets lose less AUC from development to holdout than classical ones
Home Credit logistic regression still favours mutual-information mRMR
